analysis.title: Global Performance Monitor: Narrow reversal
key_insights: MSCI AC World fell -1.7% in October after -1.3% in September, on concerns about the scale and funding of AI capex, higher oil prices and hawkish central banks. YTD the index is +9.9%.

Weakness was concentrated. Two sectors fell more than 10% while 9 of 16 global sectors rose. Energy (+11.6%), Consumer Staples (+9.9%) and Health Care (+9.2%) led. Media (-14.7%), Semiconductors (-13.3%) and Tech Hardware (-5.4%) lagged.
Europe (+0.3% in USD) was the only region to rise. Emerging Markets fell -8.1%, led lower by Korea (-15.6%) and Brazil (-12.1%).

Among 22 global themes, Consulting (+15.3%), SaaS (+11.0%) and Cybersecurity (+5.3%) were the best in October. Photonics (-21.6%), AI Compute (-17.9%) and Data Centers (-16.8%) fell most as AI-related themes sold off.
YTD theme leaders remain AI Compute (+58%), Photonics (+56%) and Data Centers (+30%), so October was a reversal against YTD leadership.
Semiconductors (-13.3%) and Tech Hardware (-5.4%) fell in October but remain among the best global sectors YTD (+34.1% and +35.2%). Energy (+11.6%) is now the best YTD sector at +45.7%.
Media & Entertainment was the worst sector in October (-14.7%) and is the worst YTD (-14.6%).

US large-cap tech lagged. NASDAQ 100 fell -6.7% and NASDAQ Composite -5.3% in October, versus S&P 500 -0.9% and Russell 2000 +0.5% in local currency. The US sector matrix shows Semiconductors -13.6%, Media -16.0% and Energy +13.9%.
Nvidia, Alphabet-A, Meta, Intel and Micron were the largest negative stock contributors to ACWI in October. Eli Lilly, Apple, Tesla and Exxon Mobil were the largest positive contributors.
Asia tech weakness: Korea fell -15.6% in USD and Taiwan -8.4% in October. Korea semiconductors fell -19.1% and Korea hardware -14.4%. Korea remains +65.0% YTD and Taiwan +54.3%.
Japan fell -4.2% in USD in October. The Nikkei 225 fell -5.2% and TOPIX -3.5% in local currency.
Seasonality (1988-2025): the fourth quarter has historically had the best average returns for World and EM equities, and November is the best month for MSCI USA.
risk_factors: Concerns about the scale and funding of AI capex drove the October selloff in AI-related themes and semiconductors.
Higher oil prices and hawkish central banks were cited as headwinds for global equities.
